column1: # The shared boundary tests (tests/boundary.py), in this language: up and down are the script a case becomes, @V@ the value written here, @ID@ the case. A case with no v: line is one this language cannot write. @NL@ is a newline.

column2: local ok = pcall(refuse, "x"); if ok then echo("returned") else echo("caught") end

column1: # The other direction (tests/boundary.py run-invoke): scripts that export functions for the host to call. x:make returns @V@; x:back hands its argument back.

column2: local n = 0@NL@export("count", function() n = n + 1; return n end)@NL@export("boom", function() error("boom") end)
export("spin", function() while true do end end)
export("hush", function() debug.sethook(); while true do end end)
for i = 0, 299 do export("f" .. i, function() return i end) end
